title: Rauw Alejandro Turns His Past, Present & Future Into a Three-Act Spectacle at Forest Hills Stadium: ‘2027 Will Be Completely Raúl’
summary: The Puerto Rican star discussed Red Bull Chapters, a production that fused his personal history with an athletic approach to live performance.
body: Forest Hills Stadium already feels like a kind of time capsule. Tucked inside Queens, its Tudor-style cottages and intimate village-like pathways create the sensation of stepping into a storybook hidden inside New York City. On Saturday night (Sept. 5), that atmosphere became the setting for Rauw Alejandro’s own living storybook: a three-act performance that moved from the Puerto Rican roots and musical influences that shaped him to the superstar he is now — and the artist he is still becoming. The show — Red Bull Chapters featuring Rauw Alejandro — was initially scheduled for one night. After that date sold out quickly, a second performance was added for Sunday (Sept. 6), giving the event an unexpected momentum even before its first chapter began. It also marked Red Bull’s first Chapters project centered on a recording artist, following the brand’s long history of building platforms around athletes, action sports and culture — including its influential Red Bull Batalla freestyle competition. That distinction mattered. This was not simply a Rauw Alejandro concert with Red Bull branding layered onto it. The production asked what might happen when Rauw’s theatrical concert language …

title: Rod Wave Achieves Fourth No. 1 Album on Billboard 200 With ‘Don’t Look Down’
summary: Plus, Alex Warren’s WILDCHILD debuts at No. 2.
body: Rod Wave earns his fourth No. 1 album on the Billboard 200 chart as Don’t Look Down debuts atop the list dated Sept. 12. The set earned 99,000 equivalent album units in the United States in its first week, ending Sept. 3, according to Luminate, largely driven by streaming activity. He previously led the list with Nostalgia (in 2023), Beautiful Mind (2022) and SoulFly (2021). Also in the top 10, Alex Warren notches his second top 10 and highest-charted set yet as WILDCHILD opens at No. 2. The Billboard 200 chart ranks the most popular albums of the week in the U.S. based on multi-metric consumption as measured in equivalent album units, compiled by Luminate. Units comprise album sales, track equivalent albums (TEA) and streaming equivalent albums (SEA). Each unit equals one album sale, or 10 individual tracks sold from an album, or 2,500 ad-supported or 1,000 paid/subscription on-demand official audio and video streams generated by songs from an album. The new Sept. 12, 2026-dated chart will be posted in full on Billboard ‘s website on Sept. 9 (a day later than usual due to the Labor Day holiday in the U.S. on Sept 7). For all chart news, follow @billboard and @billboardchart…

title: 14 Concertgoers Hospitalized at The Chainsmokers’ San Jose Show
summary: The duo took the stage at Discovery Meadow on Sept. 4.
body: More than a dozen concertgoers were hospitalized following The Chainsmokers ’ recent Bay Area show. Fourteen people were transported to local hospitals during and after the electronic duo’s outdoor concert at Discovery Meadow in San Jose, California, on Friday (Sept. 4), according to police and the San Jose Fire Department (SJFD). “At 8:22 p.m. on Friday, September 4, the San José Fire Department responded to an outdoor concert at Discovery Meadow for reports of multiple patients requiring medical attention,” the SJFD wrote on X . The fire department continued, “SJFD immediately requested an Ambulance Task Force, two additional advanced life support fire units, and a Battalion Chief to manage the incident and provide additional medical resources. A total of 14 ambulances responded, and 14 patients were transported to local hospitals.” At least 10 attendees were taken to the hospital during the final 30 minutes of the show, according to ABC 7 . Paramedics treated other concertgoers at the venue as the medical response continued through the end of the concert. title: Jay-Z Brings 30 Years of Hits to London: 9 Best Moments From His Triumphant Return
summary: The rap icon touched down in London for the second night of a Tottenham Hotspur Stadium double-header (Sept. 5).
body: Jay-Z has spent his summer making a case for his legacy. In July, he took over New York’s Yankee Stadium for three nights, celebrating 30 years of debut LP Reasonable Doubt , 25 years of The Blueprint and the defining hits that have stapled his career. Across the shows, the rapper was joined by an eye-watering selection of hip-hop and pop heavyweights, with Beyoncé, Alicia Keys, Usher, Eminem, Nas, Pharrell Williams, Rihanna and Slick Rick among the guests. Billboard ’s Angel Diaz, reporting from the run, called it “a masterclass show” — so the bar for what came next was already sky-high. Related Jay-Z Kicks Off London Shows With Beyoncé Birthday Tribute, Fugees Reunion London, for its part, is far from unfamiliar territory. Jay first came to the capital in 1989 with his mentor Jaz-O and then rocked a British crowd at Notting Hill Carnival back in 1997; by 2008 he was headlining Glastonbury’s Pyramid Stage, opening with a cover of Oasis “Wonderwall” to answer critics — including one Noel Gallagher — who didn’t think hip-hop “belonged” at the festival. title: System of a Down Release ‘Johnny’ to Streaming for the First Time
summary: The 25th anniversary Toxicity reissue also corrects a two-decade tracklist error and arrives alongside a run of stadium tour dates.
body: System of a Down has made “Johnny” available on streaming platforms for the first time, part of a wider rollout marking the 25th anniversary of Toxicity . The track had previously surfaced only on international editions of the album and a U.K. 7-inch pressed alongside “Chop Suey!,” never receiving its own standalone release until now. Toxicity arrived Sept. 4, 2001, produced by Rick Rubin, and became one of the defining metal albums of its era, fusing heavy riffing with Armenian folk influences and pointedly political lyrics addressing the environment, protest movements and U.S. foreign policy. The album debuted at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 — a chart run that fell in the week of the Sept. 11 attacks, a coincidence that shadowed the record’s early rollout, as “Chop Suey!” was pulled from radio playlists over lyrics some deemed sensitive in the moment. Lead single “Chop Suey!” nonetheless became the band’s first song to chart on the Billboard Hot 100, part of a run that saw all three of the album’s singles — “Chop Suey!,” “Toxicity” and “Aerials” — reach the chart, with “Aeri…

title: Violet Grohl Covers The Cure for Triple J’s Like a Version
summary: The singer stripped the 1992 track down to just her voice and an acoustic guitar, calling it "such a cute love song."
body: Violet Grohl delivered a stripped-down cover of The Cure’s “High” for Triple J’s Like a Version series, trading the original’s layered guitar work for a barebones acoustic arrangement built around her own vocal. “I love the childlike joy of the lyrics… it’s such a cute love song,” Grohl told Triple J of the 1992 single, the lead track from The Cure’s Wish . She said “High” has been a personal favorite for years, and traced her fandom for the band back to age 12 or 13, when hearing “Friday I’m in Love” sent her deep into their catalog. “I think it’s a perfect example of their sound during the early ’90s,” she said, “and I love all the imagery in the lyricism.” Grohl said she aimed to capture a “teenage crush kind of feeling” in the performance, adding of Cure frontman Robert Smith: “I adore Robert Smith… I would hope that they would at least think it was okay.” She also performed her own song “595,” from her debut album, in the same acoustic setting.
